question: Can two Night 6 runs be made to share an office seed, by placing the activating press at a fixed phone wall-clock residue and reading each night's seed from the game log?
whyNow: The 2026-09-15 twin nights were INCONCLUSIVE because same-residue Start taps could not be shown to share a seed: the seed itself was never measured, only the tap. Two things changed on 2026-09-16. The seed is now read from the game log to one or two milliseconds (allocRunHeader is instruction 0 of CRun.initRunLoop, so it falls between the last line logged before initRunLoop and the first logged inside it), and the tap-to-seed delay has been measured on four runs: the menu transition is tight (3612.2, 3613.6, 3614.0 ms on the Custom Night path) and all the looseness is the office load itself (1241, 1258, 1260, 1329 ms). A fixed residue therefore lands the seed in a window of roughly twenty milliseconds, and two nights collide by the birthday bound in about five to eight attempts.
predeclaredBefore: any attempt of this cohort was run

setup.binding: Night 6 h, artifacts/night6-cohort-h/bundle, unchanged -- the binding that reached 6 AM on 2026-09-13 and again on 2026-09-16
setup.anchor: NIGHT_ANCHOR_AIM_MS 4870, period 5000, maxK 0, as in both winning runs
setup.timedStart: FNAF_START_PHONE_WALL_RESIDUE_MS=20000 on every attempt, the residue the 2026-09-15 twins A and B used. The story-night path now honours it: the press that activates the focused title row is the one that loads the office frame, and it is placed when the phone's wall clock reaches the residue. A requested timed start never falls back to an untimed tap; if the first press already leaves the title there is no activating press to place and the attempt refuses.
setup.instruments: MMFRuntime logcat streamed from before each attempt (the phone's log ring rolls over in about a minute), 1280x576 video, kernel touches. Grading is deferred with --no-grade so the loop is not serialised behind an 18-minute pipeline.
setup.bound: at most 8 attempts; the loop stops at the first proven twin pair, or when an attempt cannot be returned to an observed title.

rules.seedOfAnAttempt: tools/device/office-seed-bracket.py on that attempt's streamed log, default (sourced) rule. An attempt whose log has no office load, or whose bracket cannot be formed, is void and does not count against the bound.
rules.twins: PROVEN TWINS are two attempts whose brackets are each a single millisecond and are the same millisecond. A pair whose brackets merely overlap is a CANDIDATE pair, not twins, and is reported as such.
rules.thenWhat: For a proven pair, read both nights' eyehole windows with the same reader and compare the encounter sequences. The predeclared comparison is the number of agreeing mask windows over the first 42, against the same count for every non-twin pair in the cohort. Twins that share a seed and a compiled plan should agree far more than any non-twin pair; if they do not, the seed is not what drives the night, and that is the finding.
rules.notClaimed: This measures whether the seed can be forced and whether a shared seed reproduces a night. It is not a win-rate cohort, and no rate will be quoted from it.

cohort1Result.attempts: 3 of the 8 allowed, then stopped for a measured reason (artifacts/forensics/twin-nights-night6-20260916/STOPPED.md)
cohort1Result.seeds: 24850 (1 candidate), 26756 (1), 24853 (2); all three nights died, none reached 6 AM
cohort1Result.pressPlacement: +0.030, +31.812 and +40.694 ms from the planned phone wall instant; the late two were placed while the host was busy decoding video, which is the thing to keep off the machine during a press
cohort1Result.decomposition: press to office load 3556.5, 5437.3, 3561.2 ms; office load to seed 1293.0, 1287.0, 1252.0 ms. The load is the steady part. The transition is bimodal because the title cursor survives an attempt: a press onto an already focused row activates it directly (attempts 1 and 3, 4.7 ms apart), while a press onto an unfocused row only focuses it and the untimed second press activates it 1.9 s later (attempt 2).
cohort1Result.whyStopped: The seed follows the ACTIVATING press by a steady 4849 ms, so a night the untimed second press started lands wherever that press fell. Over both modes the seeds spread 1906 ms, which needs about 55 attempts for a birthday collision. Eight could not have produced a twin, so five more nights would have bought nothing.

cohort2.change: A timed start now sends exactly one press and no second. If the row was already focused the press activates it and the night is aimed; if it was not, the press only focuses it, the night does not start, and the attempt fails in half a minute instead of playing a wrong-seeded night for eight minutes -- leaving the row focused, so the next attempt activates directly.
cohort2.expected: With every attempt on the activating path the spread is the office load's, which cohort 1 measured at 4.7 ms press-to-load and 41 ms load-to-seed. A window that wide needs about four to eight attempts.
cohort2.bound: at most 5 attempts, same residue 20000, same binding, same rules for what counts as proven twins
cohort2.hostQuiet: no video decoding or census work on this machine while an attempt is in its press window
